rules.statement: When a method has several optional inputs and must keep its CancellationToken as the last parameter, group the optional inputs into a defaultable readonly record struct with `init` properties rather than making each one a required parameter that every caller spells out as null.
rules.why: Putting the token last strips the defaults from the optional parameters, so call sites become long and repetitive and adding an optional input means editing every caller again.
rules.check: Look for methods (including test helpers) where several nullable or optional parameters come before a CancellationToken without defaults, and callers pass `x: null` for most of them.

rules.statement: Dispose a local IDisposable with a `using var` declaration rather than a `using (...) { }` block statement.
rules.why: The block form is style drift from the convention, even though the resource is still disposed.
rules.check: Look for `using (` statements wrapping a local resource such as an HttpResponseMessage or scope, in production or test code.

rules.statement: Don't pass an awaited call or another method call's result directly as an argument; hoist it into a named local first and pass the local, in test code as well as production code.
rules.why: Nesting calls such as `JsonElement.Parse(await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(ct))` or `calls.Add(GetAsync(...).AsTask())` hurts readability and makes the formatter split the call across lines, and the production code-style rules apply in tests.
rules.check: Look for `await` expressions or helper calls like `.AsTask()` written inside another call's argument list.

rules.statement: Make a collection parameter non-nullable and have callers pass an empty collection (`[]`) when null would only mean none; keep it nullable only when null has a meaning distinct from empty.
rules.why: Nullable collection inputs force the method to keep null-handling branches it wouldn't otherwise need.
rules.check: Look for `IReadOnlyDictionary<...>?`, `IEnumerable<...>?`, array or list parameters that callers pass `null` to, and check whether null means anything different from an empty collection before reporting.
